models_evaluated: scripted rule-based breast cancer screening outreach chatbot prototypes (doctor/survivor persona x direct/polite style)

links.outcome: Trust and intention to use across co-designed chatbot persona and communication style conditions vs control
links.effect: Doctor-polite persona highest trust (M=3.73 vs control 3.53, p=0.04) and intention to use (3.84 vs 3.50, p=0.04); overall ANOVA nonsignificant (trust p=0.29, intention p=0.07); some participants found persona stereotyping.
links.quote: Among the experimental conditions, the doctor-polite condition was the most preferred in terms of both trust and intention to use, compared with the control.

links.outcome: Participant perception of stereotyping in culturally tailored chatbot persona
links.effect: Some participants perceived the Black woman persona/name as stereotypical or patronizing; 11 participants across doctor groups commented on the name Ebony vs five across peer groups.
links.quote: Across doctor prototype groups, 11 participants commented that this name was stereotypical, inappropriate, patronizing, or offensive compared to five participants across peer prototype groups.

unlisted_practices: Optimizing chatbot persona and communication style (doctor vs peer, polite vs direct) to increase trust and intention to use
Using scripted rather than LLM-generated dialogs to prevent misinformation and bias
Providing option to connect with a human healthcare professional within chatbot

links.outcome: trust and intention by communication style
links.effect: Polite vs direct: intention 3.70 vs 3.49, difference −0.23, p=0.05; trust difference −0.02, p=0.72.
links.quote: Contrary to our hypothesis, we found that the direct conditions (MDirect = 3.49, SD = 1.14) resulted in a lower intention to use the chatbot compared with the polite conditions [MPolite = 3.70, SD = 1.14; difference = −0.23, t = −1.94, p = 0.05 CI (−0.46, 0.00)].

links.effect: 11 doctor-prototype vs 5 peer-prototype participants criticized the name as stereotypical, inappropriate, patronizing, or offensive.
links.quote: Across doctor prototype groups, 11 participants commented that this name was stereotypical, inappropriate, patronizing, or offensive compared to five participants across peer prototype groups.
